data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though the private frontier-tech climate sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis represents the sole applicable method. Using total capital raised of $50M as a proxy for current implied valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-round progression yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient datapoints meeting narrow stage and tier filters; only 8 same-sector peers exist, but none yielded three or more comparables at identical or adjacent stages with similar valuation tiers.

The triangulated range is $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M, derived from a single method. This single-method result introduces material uncertainty. The analysis is most sensitive to the stage multiplier assumption and to future visibility into early-stage peer outcomes in similar technology domains. Investors should treat this range as preliminary pending either accumulation of nearer-stage comps or material operating milestones from Tempo.
